title: Access, roles & sharing
intro: Internal board for the Essentials 2.0 solution concept. Not about UI: each reference shows how another product solves an access, role or sharing problem our customers actually have (learners without logins, faculty that cannot be scoped to their own students, rosters living in Canvas, eight global roles nobody needs, recordings that should open and close on dates). One section per question; every card says what we would take from it. Counter-examples are flagged. Raw material from Mobbin and Refero, to be cut down before anything is shown outside the team.

questions.title: How do products let people in without creating accounts up front (magic link, guest, identity from SSO or LMS)?
How is access scoped by content (share a course or recording with a person or group) instead of by global role?
How do products handle bulk rosters: CSV or LMS import, sync, cohorts that churn until week one?
What is the minimal role set that still has an escape hatch (owner/admin/member/guest plus per-item overrides)?
How is access time-boxed (release date, expiry, semester end, view-only links, revoke)?
How do products remove login friction and account-recovery dependency?

references.title: Welcome back (magic link primary)
references.question: Q1
references.take: Magic link is the primary CTA, password is a secondary text link, SSO is a separate block: a clear hierarchy that makes passwords the exception.

references.title: Admin login settings: SSO, provisioning, domain control
references.question: Q1
references.take: Single "Login" admin page with tabs for SSO, user provisioning and domain control — identity settings in one place.

references.title: Passwordless login to Analytics
references.question: Q1
references.take: Email-only sign-in that doubles as sign-up; "check your email" step offers mail-client shortcuts and an explicit "Logging in…" state.

references.title: Sharing a doc
references.question: Q1
references.take: An email can be granted 'Can edit' before the person exists; a 'Hasn't signed up' badge holds the seat until they arrive. Pattern for attaching a learner to a recording pre-account.

references.title: Email Login to Inbox
references.question: Q1
references.take: Six-step magic-link login with distinct "sending link" and "link sent" states — the minimum viable passwordless loop.

references.title: Accepting invite
references.question: Q1
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: 'Accept invite to view' still forces full name plus a 12-char password with 5 complexity rules, for a viewer-only invite. This is the friction that produces lockouts.

references.title: Developer account sign-up and magic-link login
references.question: Q1
references.take: One email form serves both sign-up and log-in via magic link; in-app "Verify your log-in" confirmation before landing in the dashboard.

references.title: Email Magic-Link Onboarding
references.question: Q1
references.take: Marketing CTA → auth-method card → email → link sent → empty team workspace; nothing asked beyond an email.

references.title: Team login policy: none / 2FA or SSO / SSO
references.question: Q1
references.take: Three-radio login policy (none / 2FA or SSO / SSO only) with consequence text — org-level enforcement in one control.

references.title: Accepting an invite
references.question: Q1
references.take: Invite email is already known, so 'Log in' sends a temporary magic link and drops the invitee straight into the team; no password is ever set up.

references.title: Logging in
references.question: Q1
references.take: One login screen offers Google, email magic link, SAML SSO and passkey as peers; the 'check your email' step has an 'enter code manually' fallback for when links don't open.

references.title: Sign in to Miro
references.question: Q1
references.take: 'Trouble signing in? Request a magic sign-in link' as the recovery path next to reset-password, and 'sign in to a private organization' for SSO tenants; answers the months-long lockout problem.

references.title: Continue as a visitor
references.question: Q1
references.take: Visitor mode: a shared board asks only for a display name and lets the person in; the closest analogue to attaching a learner to a recording without an account.

references.title: Passwordless sign-in & Organization Setup
references.question: Q1
references.take: "Sign in with work email" magic link lands straight in org creation — identity first, workspace second, no password anywhere.

references.title: Continue with email (sign in or create)
references.question: Q1
references.take: 'We'll sign you in or create an account if you don't have one yet': one entry point collapses login and signup so the invitee never has to know which they need.

references.title: Logging in
references.question: Q1
references.take: Email first, then 'Continue with SSO', then a 'Select an organization' picker: identity comes from the org's IdP and the user just chooses which tenant to enter.

references.title: Logging In
references.question: Q1
references.take: Magic-link login end to end, including the email itself: link expires in 20 min, single use, plus a copyable URL for signing in on a different device.

references.title: Accepting an invite
references.question: Q1
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: invite acceptance is a plain signup form (name + password) with the email pre-filled; the invite context buys nothing beyond the headline.

references.title: SSO authentication settings (admin)
references.question: Q1
references.take: Org SSO settings page: "no providers yet" empty state with one "Manage integrations" CTA — SSO as an admin toggle, invisible to end users.

references.title: Sign into workspace
references.question: Q1
references.take: Domain auto-join ('if you have an @school.edu address you can join this organization') plus a 'Send magic link' vs 'Type password' choice on the same email field.

references.title: Accepting an invitation
references.question: Q1
references.take: Three parallel ways in: a shareable join link ('anyone with this link can join'), import from Google/Slack contacts (roster source), or typed emails. Roster-import is the Canvas analogue.

references.title: Set access (document)
references.question: Q2
references.take: Attribute-scoped access on a document: Workplace x Department x Role dropdowns instead of naming people; maps to site x program x cohort for a sim center.

references.title: Sharing a project
references.question: Q2
references.take: Project-level 'Access settings' switch (My workspace vs Private to members) sits above a member list where each row carries its own role (Project admin / Editor / Viewer).

references.title: Request access to project
references.question: Q2
references.take: Denied state that routes to the project's admins (not a global admin) with an optional message for the approver; scoped access needs a scoped request path.

references.title: What can Jane Doe access?
references.question: Q2
references.take: Person-centric inverse of the share dialog: a checklist of projects one person may see, with a plain-English 'what happens next'. Direct answer to 'faculty sees only their own students'.

references.title: Share modal controls
references.question: Q2
references.take: One share modal combines link-access dropdown, collaborator invite, and per-collaborator role change/remove.

references.title: Folder sharing management
references.question: Q2
references.take: Share a document folder to a specific shareholder or group from the folder context menu — you pick a person/group, not a global role.

references.title: Project sharing & link invite
references.question: Q2
references.take: Video-project share menu: send link to recipients (autosuggest) plus separate link settings; includes share error and retry states.

references.title: Hub permissions (per-user grid)
references.question: Q2
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: per-user grid of 15 checkbox columns (view, delete own, add, archive, export...) with Users/Groups/Guests tabs; granular but unreadable, and per space rather than per content.

references.title: Folder access management
references.question: Q2
references.take: Folder "Manage access" dialog with a per-collaborator permission selector and inline confirmation of the change.

references.title: Sharing a project
references.question: Q2
references.take: Splits the audience into Collaborators vs Readers tabs, then stacks three scopes with their own level: named people, Workspace Access, Public Access.

references.title: Manage sharing and invite collaborator
references.question: Q2
references.take: Per-file share settings switch link access to "Only invited people", then invite by email — item-level scope overrides team default.

references.title: Team (User Groups)
references.question: Q2
references.take: Recording tool that sells user groups explicitly as 'easily share meetings with a particular group': groups exist to receive recordings, not to hold a global role.

references.title: Repository roles
references.question: Q2
references.take: Five pre-defined roles, each described in one sentence as 'previous role plus X', applied per repository via teams; custom roles are an escape hatch, not the default.

references.title: Invite client to workspace
references.question: Q2
references.take: External-client invite modal lets you adjust what the client can see before sending; pending invite shown in the client list.

references.title: Sharing a project
references.question: Q2
references.take: One input for 'users, groups, or collections'; the whole-workspace row is a toggle with its own level; and a 'prevent Can-edit users from re-sharing' checkbox stops privilege leaking.

references.title: Share reel: team-only vs anyone with link
references.question: Q2
references.take: Two radios — "Only members in your team" vs "Anyone with the link" — the minimal audience choice for sharing a recording.

references.title: Creating a group
references.question: Q2
references.take: People table with Teamspaces / Groups / Role as separate columns, and a Groups tab that shows how many teamspaces each group unlocks; groups are a sharing target, role stays minimal.

references.title: Share a document
references.question: Q2
references.take: Share dialog is organised by audience tab: Workspace Members (Restricted) / Guests / Everyone (No Access). Being in the workspace does not mean seeing the document.

references.title: Share document: invite with role + public link toggle
references.question: Q2
references.take: Doc-level modal: invite by email with role, list of guests vs team members, and a public-link toggle — all scoped to one document.

references.title: Roles permission matrix
references.question: Q2
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: global capability x role checkbox matrix (dozens of rows, 'Add Role' button). This is the 8-global-roles trap: it can never express 'only my students' videos'.

references.title: Invite External Collaborator
references.question: Q2
references.take: Guest invited to a single project: a "Review external access" step warns what they will see, then a permission level is chosen.

references.title: Community Access Management
references.question: Q2
references.take: Gate a content area by audience: pick which membership tiers can access the community in a modal — edtech cohort-based scoping.

references.title: Share Video project
references.question: Q2
references.take: Video-specific share: 'All admins - Can manage' as an implicit row, owner, named person with Can comment, and a separate Link privacy control; Collaborators vs Viewers counted in the comments panel.

references.title: Client Import/Export
references.question: Q3
references.take: CSV import with a "mapping required" preview state and column labels applied before a success banner on the client list.

references.title: Bulk Stakeholder Import
references.question: Q3
references.take: Auto-maps columns on upload, then validates on import attempt with row-level errors before committing.

references.title: Admin center: Groups
references.question: Q3
references.take: Admin "Groups" area organizes members by department/location with group admins — cohort structure with delegated admin.

references.title: Manage team members
references.question: Q3
references.take: Multi-select people in the roster → "Add to group" overlay — groups/cohorts built from the existing member list.

references.title: SSO & provisioning: domain verification
references.question: Q3
references.take: "SSO & provisioning" settings with domain-verification tab — directory sync is set up next to SSO, not as a separate product.

references.title: Importing members
references.question: Q3
references.take: 'Enter manually | Import CSV' is a toggle inside the same Invite wizard (not a buried settings page), with a template CSV link and tag assignment for the whole batch; answers the 'batch upload existed but nobody found it' problem.

references.title: Importing member from CSV
references.question: Q3
references.take: Bulk import page shows the invite email preview and defaults before upload, then a 'Bulk logs' table (Pending -> Completed 2/2, input + output CSV) so a tech can verify what actually landed.

references.title: Mapping fields
references.question: Q3
references.take: 3-step Upload / Map fields / Review; the review screen counts new vs existing people, warnings and errors, and offers 'add these people to a new or existing segment' — i.e. import creates the cohort in one go.

references.title: Uploading a CSV (bulk edit of workers)
references.question: Q3
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: download-edit-upload-validate-choose-review, a 4-stage wizard in a full-screen takeover; right for 300 payroll records, far too heavy for a sim tech adding a 4-10 learner group.

references.title: Admin console: Members list with status filter
references.question: Q3
references.take: Admin members table with status filter (invited/active) and Groups as a sibling nav item — roster + cohorts in one console.

references.title: Creating a teammate group
references.question: Q3
references.take: Create-group form offers both a checkbox picker of existing people AND 'Download CSV template / Import CSV' inline — small groups by hand, big cohorts by file, same screen.

references.title: Importing members
references.question: Q3
references.take: CSV import as column-mapping table (field / sample data / import as), upserts on matching email, and auto-labels the batch 'Import <date>' so the cohort is findable afterwards.

references.title: Manage members
references.question: Q3
references.take: Group page puts Add members / Bulk upload members / Download members side by side, and separates direct vs indirect (nested) members — a model for cohorts that contain sub-groups.

references.title: Invite members dialog (link, email, 'Import list' nudge)
references.question: Q3
references.take: Invite dialog surfaces bulk import as a one-line nudge under the email box ('Want to add emails in bulk? Import list') plus a domain-restricted join link — discoverability of bulk without a separate feature.

references.title: CSV User Import
references.question: Q3
references.take: Import wizard maps each CSV column to a user attribute, then ends with a post-import report of created/updated/failed rows.

references.title: Inviting team members
references.question: Q3
references.take: Paste comma-separated emails + optional 'Add to team' in one dialog; invitees appear immediately in the members table with '(Invited)' status and their team chip, so the roster exists before anyone accepts.

references.title: Invite to team: paste multiple emails
references.question: Q3
references.take: Multiline paste box for bulk emails with an "add individually" fallback — one field handles 1 or 100 invites.

references.title: Import contacts from CSV
references.question: Q3
references.take: Canonical CSV import: upload → map columns (auto then manual) → review parsed rows → importing indicator → list.

references.title: Invite teammates (link, Google/Slack contacts, emails)
references.question: Q3
references.take: Three entry paths stacked on one card: join link, pull from Google/Slack contacts, or type emails — a join link/code is the cheapest answer to a cohort that churns until week one (learners self-enrol).

references.title: Add and enroll student
references.question: Q3
references.take: Add students manually with an "enroll in course" toggle in the same modal, then import feedback and an updated roster.

references.title: Invite people to meal plan
references.question: Q3
references.take: Same invite modal supports manual emails or CSV upload; shows format error and an "imported 0 of 5" review list to fix rows.

references.title: Event registrants list with 'Sync from email list' and 'Upload CSV'
references.question: Q3
references.take: Roster header offers 'Sync from email list' next to 'Upload CSV' with an in-page progress toast; sync (continuous, from a source of truth) and upload (one-off) are distinct verbs, matching SIS/Canvas vs spreadsheet.

references.title: Manage team member permission
references.question: Q4
references.take: Change a member's permission from the row via a selector and confirm inline — no edit page.

references.title: Workspace Guest Invitation
references.question: Q4
references.take: Separate "Guests" area for external people with a restricted role — guest as a first-class, clearly bounded role.

references.title: Updating sharing permissions
references.question: Q4
references.take: Share dialog stacks audience rows — anyone with link / anyone in workspace / inherited from folder (greyed) / named people — each with Can view / comment / edit / No access; inherited rows are shown but locked.

references.title: Invite Users from Platform Settings
references.question: Q4
references.take: Role dropdown plus a "Roles help" explainer inside the invite modal; pending invites list updates in place.

references.title: Project Access Management
references.question: Q4
references.take: Per-project collaborator roles override the workspace role — the per-item escape hatch next to a small global role set.

references.title: Editing member role
references.question: Q4
references.take: Three roles (Employee / Auditor / Admin) as a segmented control with the selected role's description underneath; members table also has 'Import from spreadsheet' and a join link right in the header.

references.title: Team permissions matrix (Basic / Low / Med / High / Owner)
references.question: Q4
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: permission levels named Basic/Low/Med/High carry no meaning — the admin must read the whole grid to know what 'Med' does; role names should describe a job, not a rank.

references.title: Changing a member role
references.question: Q4
references.take: The floor: exactly two roles (Admin / Member), each with a one-line description in the dropdown, 'Remove from workspace' as the third option; role changes are a single click with a toast, no confirm.

references.title: Share space with 'Inherited' org access and explicit per-person role
references.question: Q4
references.take: Labels the org-wide row as 'Inherited' with member count while a named person has an explicit 'Administrator' override, plus a toggle to mint a guest link with its own role — three layers, one small panel.

references.title: Changing a role
references.question: Q4
references.take: Users page is split into Invited / Guests / Members sections; a role cell offers 'Convert to guest' / 'Convert to admin' / 'Remove' with a lightweight inline confirm — guest is a conversion, not a separate account type.

references.title: Inviting a guest
references.question: Q4
references.take: Per-item escape hatch on top of workspace roles: Share panel lists people (with 'Guest' badge), the teamspace, and 'General access: Everyone at <workspace>', each with its own Full access / Can edit / Can comment level.

references.title: Invite member with Guest / Member / Admin / Owner dropdown
references.question: Q4
references.take: The canonical 4-role ladder with descriptions inline at invite time: Guest 'only projects they're invited to', Member 'create and access projects', Admin 'manage members and settings', Owner 'billing and transfer'.

references.title: Add and assign employee permissions
references.question: Q4
references.take: COUNTER: role choice, then per-business, then per-permission checklist — 8 steps to add one employee; matrix explosion.

references.title: Adding a new role
references.question: Q4
references.take: Roles as cards with plain-language descriptions and head counts, plus a dashed 'Add new role' card as the escape hatch; custom role permissions are grouped by AREA with just View / Edit columns, not per-action toggles.

references.title: Invite Members
references.question: Q4
references.take: Invite modal with an expandable "view role descriptions" panel so people pick the right role without leaving the flow.

references.title: Permission groups (apps x resources x users)
references.question: Q4
references.take: COUNTER: "Permission groups" each tracking apps × resources × users — admin must reason about a 3-D matrix to answer "who can see X".

references.title: Inviting people (guest)
references.question: Q4
references.take: Switching 'Invite as' to Guest progressively reveals required channels + an expiration date; a guest is scoped to content and time — the pattern for simulated patients or visiting faculty without a dedicated global role.

references.title: Adding a role
references.question: Q4
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: roles x permissions checkbox matrix that gains a column per role and a row per action; adding 'Contributor' means auditing ~30 cells. This is what 8 global roles turns into.

references.title: Team Member Invitation and Role Assignment
references.question: Q4
references.take: Role chosen at invite time from a short fixed list with one-line descriptions — no separate role-admin step.

references.title: Workspace members: Members / Guests tabs
references.question: Q4
references.take: Members vs Guests tabs; each row shows role and license — guest is a tab, not a role-matrix column.

references.title: User Roles with View permissions
references.question: Q4
references.take: Fixed role list (Primary Owner / Owner / Author / Affiliate) with a "View permissions" expander — small set, fully transparent.

references.title: Downgrading a member
references.question: Q4
references.take: Member -> Guest downgrade opens a confirm that spells out the consequences ('can only access channels they've been invited to, can't invite members') with an explicit 'Yes, I'm absolutely sure' checkbox.

references.title: Team member roles and access
references.question: Q4
references.take: Per-member "roles and access" page: one role plus product-level access toggles — the escape hatch lives on the person, not in a matrix.

references.title: Track share and invite link
references.question: Q5
references.take: Track sharing: invite-only vs public, allow downloads, password-protect — media-specific link controls in one panel.

references.title: Manage track share link
references.question: Q5
references.take: Reset share link with a confirmation dialog — old link dies, new one issued; the simplest revoke pattern.

references.title: Share item link: expires after + available to
references.question: Q5
references.take: "Link expires after" + "Available to" (anyone / specific emails) — two dropdowns cover expiry and audience for a shared item.

references.title: View-only link panel
references.question: Q5
references.take: View-only link explicitly framed as 'allows anyone to see the file, no sign-in required', with a LIVE badge, preview of what recipients will see, password toggle and Delete link / Update link.

references.title: Share link to board - settings
references.question: Q5
references.take: Security tier for media links: 'Require name and email to view' (lightweight identification without an account), passcode, expiration date - each an independent toggle.

references.title: Share Base Public Link
references.question: Q5
references.take: Public link lives on its own "Share publicly" tab, configured separately from collaborator invites.

references.title: Share link and set permission
references.question: Q5
references.take: Switch from restricted to link-based access and choose the link's permission level in the same step, then copy.

references.title: Generating a share link
references.question: Q5
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE (with one keeper): per-field permission checklist and 1-hour default expiry are overkill for training content, but the live '59 mins' countdown ring on the published-link screen is a good way to make a time-box visible.

references.title: Adding expiration date
references.question: Q5
references.take: Publish-to-web popover lists Password / Email access / Expiration as one stack of settings with 'Never' defaults; calendar offers 'Expire on Thu, Apr 30' vs 'Never expires'; a single Unpublish button revokes, and a viewer count shows who actually used the link.

references.title: Editing share settings
references.question: Q5
references.take: Separate 'Link for editing' vs 'Link for viewing' tabs, each with its own expiration toggle+date, password and download controls; 'Restrictions apply - Modify' surfaces the constraint next to Copy link; 'Unshare file' as the revoke-all action.

references.title: Share settings
references.question: Q5
references.take: Link settings decomposed into three questions - Who can access / What can they do (View vs Edit) / Additional security - and a note that link settings do not override people already invited directly.

references.title: Create and schedule post
references.question: Q5
references.take: Schedule a membership post's publication date/time from the post editor — scheduled publish for gated content.

references.title: Scheduling an expiration date
references.question: Q5
references.take: Video share panel: expiry with quick presets (24h / 1 week / 2 weeks) plus exact date+time, passphrase toggle, and the resulting expiry shown inline as 'Dec 31 at 11:59pm' with Edit.

references.title: Scheduling a post
references.question: Q5
references.take: Publish step as a plain-language sentence ('Set it live now' vs 'Schedule for later' + date/time), then a confirmation 'Your post will be published on October 25th at 01:42' with a one-click 'Unschedule and revert to draft' undo.

references.title: Invite link creation
references.question: Q5
references.take: Admin-created invite link carries a role, a usage limit and an expiry date — cohort self-enrolment with a built-in shelf life.

references.title: Sharing settings - share the link with
references.question: Q5
references.take: The OneDrive/SharePoint model the customer asked for: audience radio (Anyone / People you choose / People with existing access), then Can edit level, expiry date field, 'Require verification' and 'Set password' in one compact sheet.

references.title: Shareable Link Creation
references.question: Q5
references.take: "Configure protections" step before the link is generated — expiry/password set up-front, not as an afterthought.

references.title: Updating link access
references.question: Q5
references.take: 'Visitor link access' is a distinct tier for people WITHOUT an account (anonymous learners): its own view/no-access level, optional password, expiration date shown as 'Expires Feb 28, 2025, 10:50 AM GMT-7', and 'Reset visitor link' to revoke by rotating the URL without touching workspace members.

references.title: Sharing a file (NordLocker)
references.question: Q5
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: terms checkbox before generating a link, a separate security code the sender must transmit out-of-band, fixed expiry you cannot change, link frozen to one file version - security that pushes work onto the sharer.

references.title: Proton Drive public link settings
references.question: Q5
references.take: Revocation written as a consequence, not a verb: 'Stop sharing - erase this link and remove everyone with access', sitting under expiration date and link password toggles.

references.title: Edit shared link: permission + expires after
references.question: Q5
references.take: Edit an existing per-recipient link: permission dropdown + "Expires after" — expiry remains editable after the link is created.

references.title: Updating content status
references.question: Q5
references.take: Course lessons carry a Draft / Published / Scheduled / Public preview status badge with a date; multi-select lessons and 'Set status for 2 selected' in bulk - the closest analogue to faculty releasing recordings on a date.

references.title: Login & security: password, passkeys, sign out all
references.question: Q6
references.take: Login & security page manages password and passkeys side by side, plus "sign out of all devices".

references.title: Logging in (email code, 'Last used' badge)
references.question: Q6
references.take: A 'Last used' badge on the sign-in method you picked last time (email vs Google vs Microsoft) - removes the 'which account did I use?' guess that causes duplicate accounts and lockouts.

references.title: SSO email check and error handling
references.question: Q6
references.take: Enter email → system checks for SSO config → clear error when the domain has no SSO — email-first routing.

references.title: Account recovery: recovery codes
references.question: Q6
references.take: Account recovery page lists masked recovery codes with remove and "+ New recovery code" — recovery as a managed inventory.

references.title: Logging in (magic link)
references.question: Q6
references.take: 'Sign in with email' as one of several login options; confirmation screen with 'Go to inbox' and an always-visible 'Back to login options' escape so a user never gets stuck on a method.

references.title: Sign-in to Content Home
references.question: Q6
references.take: After email, choose "password or one-time code" — lets users skip password recall without a reset.

references.title: Password reset via one-time code
references.question: Q6
references.take: Password reset via one-time code typed inline, no link to click — fewer context switches.

references.title: Logging In (email or Google, no password)
references.question: Q6
references.take: Minimal 'plug and play' entry: one Google button and one email field - there is no password to forget, no sign-up vs sign-in split, and 'Check your inbox' offers only Resend.

references.title: Post-login prompt - add passkey
references.question: Q6
references.take: 'Log in faster next time' banner shown right after a successful login - the moment to offer a passkey - with a dismiss X, never a blocking step.

references.title: Logging in (magic link)
references.question: Q6
references.take: Work-email-only sign in, no password field exists; after sending the link it offers 'Open your email client: Gmail / Outlook / Superhuman' buttons to close the loop in one click.

references.title: SSO sign-in with team identifier
references.question: Q6
references.take: SSO entry via team identifier with an explicit SSO-initiation error state.

references.title: Sign-in to Business Dashboard
references.question: Q6
references.take: After password + 2FA, prompt passkey enrolment so the next login is one step.

references.title: Incorrect password - send a code instead
references.question: Q6
references.take: Microsoft account (the institution's own IdP): wrong password shows 'Send a code to <email>' inline under Next - relevant because hospital/university users already live in this pattern.

references.title: Password recovery and reset
references.question: Q6
references.take: Complete recovery loop: error → enter email → loading → "instructions sent" → set new password → back in.

references.title: Two-factor authentication setup
references.question: Q6
references.take: 2FA setup shows recovery codes and requires acknowledgement before finishing — recovery set up when access is set up.

references.title: Resetting password (with one-time code escape hatch)
references.question: Q6
references.take: On 'Incorrect email address or password' the same screen offers 'Log in with a one-time code' as an OR path, and the reset itself is a 6-digit emailed code rather than a link.

references.title: Resetting password
references.question: Q6
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: vague 'Unable to verify your account' error, only exit is Forgot password -> emailed reset link -> new password -> log in again; the whole session depends on the recovery email working.

references.title: Email Code Sign-In
references.question: Q6
references.take: On password mismatch, offer an email code instead of a reset link; handles invalid code and retry.

references.title: Recover Account - link invalid or expired
references.question: Q6
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE of the expired-link dead end: 'link you followed is invalid, or it has expired' with only a text 'try again' - shows why magic links need a code fallback and a visible expiry.

references.title: Security settings - passkey recommended, secondary email
references.question: Q6
references.take: Security page ranks Passkeys 'Recommended' above Password, explains 'takes under a minute', and adds 'Secondary email - used to restore access' so recovery does not depend on one institutional mailbox.

references.title: Recover your account with recovery key
references.question: Q6
references.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: recovery depends on a key PDF saved on 'the device you used to sign up' - exactly the hidden recovery dependency that produces six-month lockouts; failure message gives no alternative.

references.title: Too many login attempts - login with code
references.question: Q6
references.take: Rate-limit dialog offers 'Login with code' as the primary way out instead of a hard lockout - the direct antidote to months-long password lockouts.

references.title: Logging in with passcode
references.question: Q6
references.take: The 'forgot password' link is rewritten as 'Forgot password? Log in with passcode' - the recovery path IS a login path (emailed code), so a forgotten password never blocks the session or requires a reset.

references.title: Create a passkey
references.question: Q6
references.take: Passkey modal explains in plain words what you will log in with (Face ID / Touch ID / Passcode); Security page also lists Recovery phone as a backup channel and current login activity.

references.title: Logging in (6-digit email code)
references.question: Q6
references.take: One-time code instead of a link (works when the email client is on another device); 'Use a different email' and a yellow nudge 'still waiting on your code? try signing up instead' handle the no-account case without a dead end.

references.title: Sign in with Google / Microsoft / LinkedIn / SSO / instant link
references.question: Q6
references.take: One screen offers every institutional path - Google, Microsoft, SSO - AND 'Email me a link to sign in instantly' as a peer of the password button, so a locked-out user has three ways in without support.
